where: Figure caption and figure aria text (also repeated idea in Section 2)
problem: The caption says the real curve 'crosses the Raoult line'. It does not. With A = 0.405 > 0 the plotted curve p₁ = x₁ exp[A(1 − x₁)²] P₁sat is larger than x₁ P₁sat for every x₁ between 0 and 1 (33.2 kPa against 30 kPa at x₁ = 0.5), so it stays above the Raoult line and only meets it at x₁ = 0 and x₁ = 1. A student looking at the figure will be confused about which curve is which and about the sign of the deviation.
fix: Write: 'The real curve leaves the origin along the steep Henry tangent (slope 90 kPa), stays above the Raoult line (slope 60 kPa) for all 0 < x₁ < 1 — positive deviation from Raoult's law — and rejoins the Raoult line only at x₁ = 1, where p₁ = P₁sat = 60 kPa.' Use the same wording in the aria text.

problem: The phrase 'but with the molecular environment and activity coefficient it would have at infinite dilution' suggests the standard state carries the value γi∞. That contradicts the Henry convention, where the standard state has activity coefficient 1 by definition and γi∞ = Hi/Pisat, which here would be 90/60 = 1.5, not 1. The rest of the answer is right; the middle clause muddles it.
fix: Answer: 'The reference is the solute at x_i = 1 with the fugacity it would have if it kept behaving as at infinite dilution all the way to x_i = 1. In that state the activity coefficient is 1 by construction and the fugacity is H_i, not P_i^sat. No real pure liquid solute has that fugacity, so the state is an extrapolation, not a physical liquid.'
